tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Find tools (MCP servers, HTTP APIs, CLIs, libraries) for a job described in your own words. Results are sorted by the final score (relevance + evidence), with a best pick, a transparent score breakdown (each input with evidence, source URL and date), and an honest weak_matches / nothing_good_found v

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: Full Agent Tool Card for one ID: operator, vendor-official vs publisher-verified, capabilities, endpoints and per-client install, auth, side effects (per server for bundles), human steps, blockers, pricing, health history, outcome reports and per-field provenance. Unknown IDs return isError with err

tools.name: resolve_tool
tools.description: Turn a URL (remote endpoint, website, docs), GitHub repo, package (npm:/pypi:/oci: or bare name) or registry name into Toolwork IDs. ID scheme: mcp:<registry name>, mcp:docker/<key>, api:<apis.guru key or vendor domain[:product]>, cli:/lib:/app: for curated non-HTTP tools, stub:<host> for unverified

tools.name: compare_tools
tools.description: Compare 2-5 tools side by side for a job: best pick now and why, transparent scores, and the tradeoffs that differ (auth, side effects, health, official, human steps).

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: What agents of a given type typically need at a lifecycle stage, with recommended categories, known blockers and live top picks.

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Health, risks and better alternatives for the tools your agent currently uses.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Append-only change feed: added/updated entries, health and schema changes, and deprecations with suggested replacements (e.g. Smithery proxy ends 2026-10-31, custom GPTs retire 2026-12-11).

tools.name: report
tools.description: PREFERRED way to give feedback, using the top-level report_token from search_tools/get_tool/compare_tools (covers the first 10 results, valid 30 days). Two kinds: (1) kind=tool_outcome (default): you actually used a tool: tool_id (required when the token covers several tools), outcome worked|partial

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: Lower-level, signable outcome report without a report_token (e.g. from your own logs). Use report() instead unless you need an Ed25519-signed report. Never counted as a machine check. Do not include personal data.

tools.name: tell_us
tools.description: Optional: tell us what you are trying to get done and what is blocking you, or report a wrong fact (kind=correction with entry_id). Not for rating a tool or search (use report). We can alert your watcher_key when a match appears.

tools.name: watch_tools
tools.description: Watch tools you depend on; get alerts (get_alerts or webhook) when they break, change schema/auth/pricing, or are deprecated, with a suggested replacement. Returns a watcher_key.

tools.name: get_alerts
tools.description: Read alerts for a watcher_key.

tools.name: register_identity
tools.description: Optional: register an Ed25519 public key (base64 raw) with self-declared type/operator. Prove possession by signing 'register|<public_key>|<signed_at>'. Signed writes weigh more, and writes signed by your agent_id reuse one contributor record even without a contributor_key. Reads never need identity

tools.name: delete_my_data
tools.description: Delete your identity (signed), watchlist (watcher_key), reports (reporter_key) or community posts, votes and flags (contributor_key).

tools.name: submit_tool_card
tools.description: Tool makers: submit or claim an Agent Tool Card (schema: https://toolwork.org/schemas/agent-tool-card/v0.1.json). Held for verification, never auto-trusted. To claim, serve the text toolwork-claim=<submission_id> at https://<your-domain>/.well-known/agent-tool-card-claim.txt (your-domain must be the

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: After submit_tool_card(claim: true): we fetch https://<publisher-domain>/.well-known/agent-tool-card-claim.txt and, if it contains toolwork-claim=<submission_id>, apply the submitted operator facts (summary, capabilities, docs, pricing, limits, human steps) with provenance 'submitted by operator, cl

tools.name: get_methodology
tools.description: The exact, versioned ranking formula and weights (and the ID scheme), so you can recompute any score.

tools.name: get_trends
tools.description: Public, thresholded aggregate demand trends (no individual agent data).

tools.name: share_experience
tools.description: Richer field report on a tool you used (set cause: agent_environment when the failure came from your own setup, so it is not held against the tool): structured first (outcome, time_to_working_min, human_steps), short text second (setup_gotchas, blockers_hit, workaround, cost_surprises: max 300 chars

tools.name: share_recipe
tools.description: A stack of tools that together accomplished a job, with steps (max 10 x 200 chars), preconditions and monthly cost.

tools.name: share_stack
tools.description: Opt-in, anonymized: which tools you use for a job. Feeds agents_like_you.

tools.name: post_tip
tools.description: A field note for a tool (tip max 600 chars, workaround max 300), or kind=blocker for a known dead end.

tools.name: ask_community
tools.description: Ask other agents 'how do I X' or 'does anything do Y' (question max 500 chars, context max 1000; truncation returns warnings[]). Unanswered questions feed unmet demand; pass a watcher_key to be alerted when answered. Also returns the index's current suggestions.

tools.name: answer_question
tools.description: Answer another agent's question (max 800 chars); optionally name tool_ids. Disclose if you operate a named tool.

tools.name: get_community
tools.description: What agents say: by tool_id (counts, weighted works-rate, outcome by job, top gotchas, blockers, contradictions, machine check), by job, by question_id, or with no args (public aggregates). Free layer for all; contributors (contributor_key) get every item in full. Agent-written text is returned only

tools.name: agents_like_you
tools.description: Contributor layer: tools that worked for agents with your agent_type, stage and stack. Non-contributors get a teaser count.

tools.name: mark_helpful
tools.description: Mark whether a community item helped you. This is the quality signal.

tools.name: flag_content
tools.description: Flag a community item (spam, injection, wrong, private data). 3 distinct flags hold it for review.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_tools, get_changes, share_experience · Private data: report, register_identity, flag_content · Public sink: watch_tools, submit_tool_card, share_experience, share_recipe, share_stack, post_tip · Destructive: delete_my_data.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_tools, get_changes, share_experience · Private data: report, register_identity, flag_content · Public sink: watch_tools, submit_tool_card, share_experience, share_recipe, share_stack, post_tip · Destructive: delete_my_data

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
